subject.title: fix: suppress exec-like tool error warnings regardless of includeDetails

question: Should exec-like tool errors with `includeDetails` bypass mutating-warning handling, or should cron, heartbeat, full-verbose, timeout, and assistant-claimed-success exec failures remain visibly warned?
rationale: Current tests encode useful visible-warning behavior, while the PR and linked issue request broad suppression; automation should not choose that product boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Preserve visible failure-detail contexts
options.body: Keep cron, heartbeat, full-verbose, timeout, and claimed-success exec warnings visible, then narrow the linked issue or patch to only the unwanted benign leak.

options.title: Suppress exec-like details earlier
options.body: Move exec-like suppression ahead of mutating handling and update tests to make the broad suppression behavior explicit.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the PR open until the contributor supplies proof and a maintainer confirms the warning policy.

recommendation.title: Preserve visible failure-detail contexts
recommendation.body: Keep cron, heartbeat, full-verbose, timeout, and claimed-success exec warnings visible, then narrow the linked issue or patch to only the unwanted benign leak.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the clearest history across the shared helper and merged exec-warning behavior that define the policy boundary.
